name: Agents definition
description:
1. **Request:** introduce an independent agent in codx-junior that works, refines and tests until a task is done, with behaviour defined by `Profile` (guardrails, budget and tool limits reused) and the ability to interact with the user.
2. **First deliverable:** reviewed the existing runtime (`SmolAgent`, `LoopGuard`, `AgentRunContext`, `ChatEventBridge`, `GuardrailService`) and drafted the AgentEngine two-level loop (plan → step → verify → decide) with diagrams, plus `agents/models.py`, `agents/policy.py` and `Profile.agent` / `AgentSettings` schemas.
3. **Refinements requested:** HITL at stopper conditions (declared by profile **and** main task), one Kanban task per agent step on the main task's board, chat mode `agent` as the trigger (with concerns), a hierarchical budget where all sub-task costs cannot exceed the main task budget, and pause/stop/resume semantics.
4. **Second deliverable:** updated the design with new sections for triggering, per-step task tracking with status sync, the budget tree (`available = limit − own − children − reserved`), stopper condition catalogue with resolution precedence and dialogue sequence, and pause/stop/resume contracts with API surface — plus `PAUSED` state, `AgentBudget`, `AgentStopperRule`, `AgentStepTask`, `AgentPause`, `Chat.agent_task` and `Chat.agent_run`.
5. **Status:** design only — `AgentSettings.enabled` defaults to `false`; three open points (step-card creation timing, own vs rolled-up `Chat.cost`, one-step plans for trivial requests) await confirmation before phase 2 (`engine.py`, `state_store.py`, `tasks.py`, agent tools).

messages.content:
Time to introduce agents in codx-junior.
We need a independent agent that can perform complex tasks based on user requests and work, refine, and test until task is done.
At some point agents must be able to interact with user.
Review all current stuff in codx-junior and start drafting the AgentEngine, Agents behavior will be defined by Profile. We alrteady have guardrails and top budged, tool limits, ...see if we need more settings.

----

As an example of what we expect to achieve: "An agent should be able to perform like a human will do"

So Agents can use tools, create more tasks, and continue until having work done or stopper condition.

----

Add diagrams to the design to validate the approach

I'll start by reviewing the existing agent runtime, guardrails, settings, and related infrastructure before drafting the AgentEngine design.## 1. Review & Understand the Task **Objective** - Introduce an **independent agent** in codx-junior capable of performing complex user requests end-to-end: work → refine → test, until done or a stopper condition is hit. - Behaviour must be **defined by `Profile`** (already exists). - Must **interact with the user** at some point (blocking, resumable). - Must reuse what already exists: guardrails, cost budget, tool limits, event runtime, persistence. - Deliver a **design draft with diagrams** so the approach can be validated before implementation. - Identify **what settings are missing** beyond what exists today. **Acceptance criteria for this turn** - A reviewable design document with mermaid diagrams (architecture, loops, state machine, HITL, budgets, persistence). - Concrete, typed models + policy resolution (small, dependency-free, testable) so the design is anchored in code. - Explicit list of settings we have vs settings we need. - No behaviour change to existing chat flows. ## 2. Information Gathering (summary of what I found) | Building block | File | Reusable as-is | |---|---|---| | Inner LLM/tool loop | `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py` | ✅ the agent's **inner loop** | | Run events / cancellation / analytics | `engine/agent_runtime.py` (`AgentRunContext`, `AgentEventType`) | ✅ + needs new step events | | Crash-safe message persistence | `codx/junior/chat/chat_event_bridge.py` | ✅ attach step events like `tool_events` | | Merge-safe persistence + chat budget | `chat_manager.py` (`add_message`, `update_message`, `Chat.cost`) | ✅ | | Loop protection | `ai/smol/loop_guard.py` | ✅ per-step limits | | Cost typing | `model/agent.py` (`AgentRunResult`, `CostInfo`) | ✅ | | Guardrails | `guardrails/service.py` (`check_input`, `check_output`, `check_tool`, `filter_tools`) | ✅ + per-tool-call enforcement | | Behaviour definition | `model/profile.py` (`Profile`, `ProfileGuardrailSettings`) | ✅ extend with `Profile.agent` | | Global agent settings | `model/model.py` → `AgentSettings.max_agent_iteractions = 4` | ⚠️ too thin | | Tools registry | `tools/__init__.py`, `tools/model.py` (`ToolSettings.scope`, `dual_response`) | ✅ + agent-only tools | | Task creation | `tools/create_task_tool.py`, `process_task_tool.py` | ✅ sub-tasks | | Verification | `engine/code_engine.py` → `project_script_test()` (`settings.script_test`, `script_test_check_regex`) | ✅ | | Legacy agent loop | `chat_engine.py` (`CHAT_MODE_AGENT` + `AGENT_DONE_WORD` recursion, max 4 iterations) | ❌ to be **replaced** | | Legacy agents package | `codx/junior/agents/{base,devops,git_issues}_agent.py` | ⚠️ legacy, not the engine | **Key conclusion:** the "hard" parts (streaming, tools, cost, cancellation, crash-safe persistence, guardrails) already exist. What is missing is (a) an **outer loop** with a persisted plan/step state machine, (b) a **human-in-the-loop suspension/resume** mechanism, (c) a **step-level verification** loop, and (d) **richer settings**. ## 3. Change Proposal Two-level execution model: - **Outer loop = `AgentEngine`** — plan → step → verify → decide → next step. Bounded by steps, cost, wall clock, sub-tasks. - **Inner loop = `SmolAgent`** — LLM rounds + tool calls inside a single step (unchanged, bounded by `LoopGuard`). Everything else is reused: `AgentRunContext` (events/cancel), `ChatEventBridge` (persistence), `GuardrailService`, `Chat.cost`/`estimation_cost`, `ToolResponse` dual response (user answer vs LLM feedback), `create_task` for sub-tasks, `project_script_test()` for verification. **Risks / edge cases handled in the design:** resume after restart, duplicate resume, agent asking while a step is half-done, budget exhausted mid-step, guardrail blocking one tool, provider failure inside a step, legacy `agent` mode replacement. ### Files | File | Type | Why | |---|---|---| | `codx/junior/agents/README.md` | new | Design document with diagrams (main deliverable) | | `codx/junior/agents/models.py` | new | Typed agent-run state machine models | | `codx/junior/agents/policy.py` | new | Resolve effective limits/behaviour from Profile + GlobalSettings + Chat budget | | `codx/junior/model/profile.py` | update | `AgentBehavior`, `AgentVerificationSettings`, `AgentAskUserSettings`; `Profile.agent` | | `codx/junior/model/model.py` | update | Extend global `AgentSettings` with the missing defaults | ## 4. Changes Summary 1. **`agents/README.md`** — full design: inventory, architecture, Profile-driven behaviour, two-level loop, state machine, planning/verification, HITL suspend/resume, sub-tasks, memory, limits/stop conditions, guardrails, events/persistence, settings gap analysis, module layout/API, phases, open questions. All with mermaid diagrams. *(new file, self-contained)* 2. **`agents/models.py`** — `AgentRunStatus`, `AgentStopReason`, `AgentStepStatus`, `AgentStep`, `AgentPlan`, `AgentQuestion`, `AgentVerification`, `AgentLimits`, `AgentUsage`, `AgentPolicy`, `AgentRunState`, `AgentRunSummary`. Pure data, no side effects. 3. **`agents/policy.py`** — `resolve_agent_policy(settings, profile, chat)` / `resolve_agent_limits(...)`: global defaults → narrowed by `Profile.agent` (min-rule unless `allow_limit_overrides`) → clamped by the chat budget (`Chat.estimation_cost - Chat.cost`) and by the profile tool allowlist. 4. **`model/profile.py`** — adds the `agent` block to `Profile` (role, planning, limits, verification, ask-user, confirm-tools). Defaults keep every existing profile unchanged. 5. **`model/model.py`** — `AgentSettings` keeps `max_agent_iteractions` and gains the global agent defaults (steps, rounds, cost, wall clock, sub-tasks, concurrency, questions, timeouts, retention). ## 5. The Changes # AgentEngine — autonomous agents for codx-junior > **Status: design draft — no runtime behaviour implemented yet.** > > This document is the review artifact for the first iteration of the > **AgentEngine**. It inventories what already exists, proposes the > architecture, the state machine, the interaction model with the user, the > limits/settings that are missing, and the implementation phases. > > Two supporting modules ship with this draft so the design is anchored in > reviewable code: > > * `codx/junior/agents/models.py` — typed state machine models > * `codx/junior/agents/policy.py` — effective limits/behaviour resolution > > plus the schema extensions `Profile.agent` and `AgentSettings`. --- ## Contents 1. [Objective](#1-objective) 2. [Scope of this draft](#2-scope-of-this-draft) 3. [What already exists](#3-what-already-exists) 4. [Concepts](#4-concepts) 5. [Architecture](#5-architecture) 6. [Behaviour is defined by Profile](#6-behaviour-is-defined-by-profile) 7. [The two-level loop](#7-the-two-level-loop) 8. [Run state machine](#8-run-state-machine) 9. [Planning](#9-planning) 10. [Step execution & decision](#10-step-execution--decision) 11. [Verification](#11-verification) 12. [Interaction with the user](#12-interaction-with-the-user-human-in-the-loop) 13. [Creating more work (sub-tasks)](#13-creating-more-work-sub-tasks) 14. [Memory & context](#14-memory--context) 15. [Limits, budgets & stop conditions](#15-limits-budgets--stop-conditions) 16. [Guardrails](#16-guardrails) 17. [Events, persistence & crash safety](#17-events-persistence--crash-safety) 18. [Settings: what we have vs what we need](#18-settings-what-we-have-vs-what-we-need) 19. [Module layout & API](#19-module-layout--api) 20. [Implementation phases](#20-implementation-phases) 21. [Open questions](#21-open-questions) --- ## 1. Objective > "An agent should be able to perform like a human will do." A human working on a task: 1. reads the request and the code, 2. writes down a **plan** (steps with a verifiable outcome each), 3. **works** one step at a time with tools (search, read, edit, run), 4. **verifies** (tests, build, lint, re-read the diff), 5. if verification fails → **refines** and retries (bounded), 6. if something is ambiguous or destructive → **asks** the user, 7. keeps **notes** so context is not lost while the conversation grows, 8. when the plan is done and verified → **reports** and closes the task. The AgentEngine must do exactly this, using the existing chat, tools, guardrails and budget infrastructure — and it must stop deterministically when something is wrong (no silent infinite work). ## 2. Scope of this draft **In scope (this draft)** * Architecture and state machine. * Behaviour definition through `Profile`. * Effective-limit resolution (`agents/policy.py`) and the missing settings. * Human-in-the-loop suspend/resume contract. * Event/persistence contract on top of `AgentRunContext` + `ChatEventBridge`. **Out of scope (later phases)** * The `AgentEngine` runtime itself, agent-only tools (`ask_user`, `agent_plan`, `run_verification`), API endpoints and the client UI. * Multi-agent orchestration (agent A delegating to agent B beyond sub-tasks). * Replacing the legacy `codx/junior/agents/*_agent.py` modules. ## 3. What already exists The inner machinery is already in place; the AgentEngine is an **outer loop** on top of it. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph EXISTING["Already implemented"] SA["SmolAgent
LLM rounds + tools"] LG["LoopGuard
rounds / calls / stuck"] TC["ToolCache
per-chat dedup"] ARC["AgentRunContext
events / cancel / analytics"] CEB["ChatEventBridge
crash-safe persistence"] CM["ChatManager
merge-safe writes"] GS["GuardrailService
input / output / tool"] TOOLS["TOOLS registry
scope + dual response"] COST["Chat.cost / estimation_cost
+ AgentRunResult.CostInfo"] end subgraph MISSING["Missing — this draft"] AE["AgentEngine
plan / step / verify / decide"] STATE["AgentRunState
persisted"] HITL["ask_user
suspend + resume"] VER["verification loop"] end AE --> SA SA --> LG SA --> TC SA --> ARC ARC --> CEB CEB --> CM AE --> GS SA --> TOOLS AE --> STATE AE --> HITL AE --> VER SA --> COST ``` | Building block | Location | Role in the engine | |---|---|---| | `SmolAgent.chat()` | `ai/smol/smol_agent.py` | Executes **one step** (one LLM/tool run) and returns a typed `AgentRunResult` | | `LoopGuard` | `ai/smol/loop_guard.py` | Depth / breadth / stuck-loop guard **inside a step** | | `ToolCache` | `ai/smol/tool_cache.py` | Avoids re-executing identical tool calls | | `AgentRunContext` | `engine/agent_runtime.py` | Event fan-out, cancellation, run analytics | | `ChatEventBridge` | `chat/chat_event_bridge.py` | Attaches events to the response message, persists on every change | | `ChatManager` | `chat_manager.py` | `add_message` / `update_message`, monotonic `Chat.cost` | | `GuardrailService` | `guardrails/service.py` | Input/output/tool policy, deterministic decisions | | `TOOLS` / `ToolSettings` | `tools/__init__.py`, `tools/model.py` | `scope`, `dual_response`, `project_settings`, `session` | | `create_task` / `process_task` | `tools/*_task_tool.py` | Sub-task creation (child chats) | | `project_script_test()` | `engine/code_engine.py` | Project verification command | | `Profile` / `ProfileGuardrailSettings` | `model/profile.py` | **Behaviour definition** | | `AgentSettings` | `model/model.py` | Global agent defaults (currently only `max_agent_iteractions`) | ### What must be replaced `ChatEngine` today implements "agent mode" as a **recursive chat loop**: ```python # chat_engine.py (legacy) is_agent_done = AGENT_DONE_WORD in response_message.content if is_agent and not is_agent_done and iterations_left: return await self._chat_with_project_inner(..., iteration=iteration + 1) ``` Problems: no plan, no verification, no user interaction, no per-step limits, no persisted state, the stop word is a magic string inside the answer, and the loop restarts the whole prompt building each iteration. **The AgentEngine replaces that recursion.** `CHAT_MODE_AGENT` becomes an entry point into `AgentEngine.run()`; `AGENT_DONE_WORD` is kept only for backward compatibility and is superseded by the structured decision (`action=finish`). ## 4. Concepts | Concept | Definition | Persisted | |---|---|---| | **Agent** | An autonomous worker. Its behaviour is a `Profile` (`Profile.agent` + tools + guardrails + model). | Profile files | | **Agent Run** | One execution of an agent over one chat goal. Identified by `run_id`. | `AgentRunState` + `Chat.agent_run` | | **Goal** | The user's request, normalised into one sentence + assumptions. | `AgentPlan.goal` | | **Plan** | Ordered list of `AgentStep`s with a verifiable outcome each. Revisable. | `AgentPlan` | | **Step** | One unit of work executed by **one `SmolAgent` run**. | `AgentStep` | | **Verification** | Deterministic check of a step (project script, build, lint, or LLM review). | `AgentVerification` | | **Question** | A blocking request for user input (`ask_user` tool). | `AgentQuestion` | | **Note** | Free-form agent memory that survives context compaction. | `AgentRunState.notes` | | **Policy** | The *effective* limits/behaviour resolved for a run. | `AgentPolicy` (derived, not persisted) | | **Stop reason** | Why the run stopped. Always exactly one. | `AgentStopReason` | ## 5. Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD U["User message"] --> CE["ChatEngine
context + knowledge + profiles"] CE --> PRE{"mode == agent?
and policy.enabled"} PRE -->|no| SMOL["SmolAgent
(single-run chat)"] PRE -->|yes| AE["AgentEngine.run()"] AE --> RESUME{"pending question
for this chat?"} RESUME -->|yes| ANS["Consume answer
resume step"] RESUME -->|no| PLAN["Plan phase
LLM → AgentPlan"] ANS --> LOOP PLAN --> LOOP LOOP["Step loop"] --> POLICY["AgentPolicy
limits / tools / verification"] LOOP --> STEP["Step execution
SmolAgent + tools"] STEP --> ARC["AgentRunContext
TOOL_* / STEP_* / LLM_* events"] ARC --> CEB["ChatEventBridge
persist + stream"] STEP --> ASK{"ask_user called?"} ASK -->|yes| SUSP["Suspend: NEEDS_INPUT
persist AgentRunState"] ASK -->|no| VER["Verify step"] VER -->|failed & attempts left| STEP VER -->|ok| DEC["Decision
continue / replan / finish"] DEC -->|continue| LOOP DEC -->|replan| PLAN DEC -->|finish| DONE["COMPLETED
report + close task"] DEC -->|stop condition| STOP["Terminal state
BUDGET / LIMIT / NO_PROGRESS / ..."] ``` The engine never talks to the provider directly: **every LLM interaction goes through `SmolAgent`**, which keeps streaming, cost accounting, events, cancellation and tool execution in one place. ## 6. Behaviour is defined by Profile An agent **is** a profile. Nothing is hardcoded in the engine. ```mermaid classDiagram class Profile { +str name +str description +str content +str parsed_content +List~str~ tools +List~str~ profiles +str llm_model +str chat_mode +ProfileGuardrailSettings guardrails +AgentBehavior agent } class AgentBehavior { +bool enabled +str role +str system +bool plan_required +int max_steps +int max_rounds_per_step +float max_cost_cxjcoins +int max_wall_clock_seconds +int max_sub_tasks +bool allow_limit_overrides +List~str~ confirm_tools +AgentVerificationSettings verification +AgentAskUserSettings ask_user } class AgentVerificationSettings { +bool enabled +str strategy +str script +str success_regex +int max_attempts +bool llm_review +str review_model } class AgentAskUserSettings { +bool enabled +List~str~ when +int timeout_seconds +str on_timeout +str default_answer +int max_questions_per_run } Profile --> AgentBehavior AgentBehavior --> AgentVerificationSettings AgentBehavior --> AgentAskUserSettings ``` Three layers define a run, from general to specific: | Layer | Where | Character | |---|---|---| | **Capabilities** | `Profile.tools`, `Profile.profiles` (linked), `Profile.llm_model` | what the agent *can* do | | **Safety** | `Profile.guardrails` (`scope`, `allowed_tools`, `risk_threshold`, `refusal_message`) | what it *must not* do | | **Behaviour** | `Profile.agent` (`role`, planning, limits, verification, ask-user) | how it *works* | Example profile (`software_developer` + agent behaviour): ```json { "name": "software_developer", "category": "coding", "llm_model": "gpt-4o", "tools": ["project_search", "project_read_file", "apply_file_changes", "project_structure", "get_file_last_version", "run_verification"], "guardrails": { "enabled": true, "allowed_tools": ["project_search", "project_read_file", "apply_file_changes"] }, "agent": { "enabled": true, "role": "Senior engineer implementing a request in an existing codebase", "plan_required": true, "max_steps": 10, "max_rounds_per_step": 12, "verification": { "enabled": true, "strategy": "project_script", "max_attempts": 2 }, "ask_user": { "enabled": true, "when": ["blocked", "ambiguous", "destructive"], "timeout_seconds": 900 }, "confirm_tools": ["apply_file_changes"] } } ``` --- ## 7. The two-level loop ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph OUTER["Outer loop — AgentEngine (steps)"] O1["Evaluate stop conditions"] --> O2{"stop?"} O2 -->|yes| O3["Terminal state + report"] O2 -->|no| O4["Take next step from plan"] O4 --> O5["Run inner loop for the step"] O5 --> O6["Verify step"] O6 --> O7["Decision: continue / replan / ask / finish"] O7 --> O1 end subgraph INNER["Inner loop — SmolAgent (LLM rounds)"] I1["Build OpenAI messages"] --> I2["Stream completion"] I2 --> I3{"tool_calls?"} I3 -->|yes| I4["LoopGuard.check"] I4 --> I5["Execute tools
TOOL_START / END / ERROR"] I5 --> I2 I3 -->|no| I6["Return AgentRunResult"] end O5 -.-> I1 I6 -.-> O6 ``` | Loop | Owner | Guards | Produces | |---|---|---|---| | Inner (rounds) | `SmolAgent` + `LoopGuard` | `max_iterations`, `max_tool_calls`, `max_identical_rounds`, `ToolCache` | `AgentRunResult` (content, cost, tool summaries) | | Outer (steps) | `AgentEngine` | `AgentPolicy.limits` + stop conditions | `AgentRunState` + final answer | **Why two levels?** A single step frequently needs many tool rounds (search → read 5 files → patch → re-read). But a step must be *abandonable*: when a step fails verification twice, the engine discards it, replans and continues — something a flat tool loop cannot express. ### Prompt budget per step Each step starts a **fresh, compact** conversation: ```text system → profile content + agent role + plan summary + notes + step objective user → current step objective, relevant files, previous step results tools → policy.tools (profile tools ∩ guardrail allowlist) ``` This keeps every step cheap and prevents the classic "context explosion" of a 40-round recursion (the legacy `agent` mode rebuilt the whole prompt each iteration and paid for the full history each time). ## 8. Run state machine ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> PENDING PENDING --> PLANNING: goal accepted PLANNING --> RUNNING: plan created PLANNING --> NEEDS_INPUT: plan needs clarification RUNNING --> VERIFYING: step finished VERIFYING --> RUNNING: verification failed (retry) VERIFYING --> RUNNING: next step VERIFYING --> PLANNING: replan required RUNNING --> NEEDS_INPUT: ask_user PLANNING --> NEEDS_INPUT: ask_user NEEDS_INPUT --> RUNNING: user answered RUNNING --> COMPLETED: plan done + verified PLANNING --> BLOCKED: guardrail / impossible RUNNING --> BLOCKED: guardrail / missing dependency RUNNING --> BUDGET_EXCEEDED: cost limit RUNNING --> LIMIT_EXCEEDED: steps / rounds / wall clock RUNNING --> NO_PROGRESS: repeated identical decisions RUNNING --> CANCELLED: user cancelled RUNNING --> FAILED: provider / unrecoverable error COMPLETED --> [*] BLOCKED --> [*] BUDGET_EXCEEDED --> [*] LIMIT_EXCEEDED --> [*] NO_PROGRESS --> [*] CANCELLED --> [*] FAILED --> [*] ``` Mapping to persisted fields: | State | `AgentRunState.status` | `Chat.status` | `AgentStopReason` | |---|---|---|---| | Planning | `planning` | `in_progress` | — | | Working | `running` | `in_progress` | — | | Verifying | `verifying` | `in_progress` | — | | Waiting for user | `waiting_user` | `waiting_user` | `needs_input` | | Done | `finished` | `done` | `completed` | | Budget/limit/no-progress/blocked/failed | `finished` | `blocked` | matching value | `Chat.status` transitions are already recorded in `Chat.status_history` by `ChatManager.save_chat()`, so agent runs automatically feed the task metrics. ## 9. Planning Planning is a **single, cheap LLM call** (`temperature=0`) that must return JSON only (parsed with the existing `extract_json_blocks` helper). ```json { "goal": "Add pagination to /api/chats and update the client list view", "assumptions": ["REST, not GraphQL", "no DB migration needed"], "steps": [ { "title": "Locate the chats endpoint", "objective": "Find the route and its query handling", "verification": "none" }, { "title": "Implement pagination parameters", "objective": "Add page/page_size with defaults and validation", "verification": "project_script" }, { "title": "Update the client list view", "objective": "Send page/page_size and render the pager", "verification": "project_script" } ] } ``` Rules enforced by the engine (not by the prompt): * `max_steps` → reject/clip plans that are too long. * `plan_required=false` → skip planning, the first step is the goal itself. * A plan is **revisable**: the decision `replan` rewrites `AgentPlan` and increments `AgentPlan.revision` (bounded by `max_steps` overall, not per plan). * Nothing is planned for files the agent is not allowed to touch (`guardrails.allowed_tools`). ## 10. Step execution & decision Each step is one `SmolAgent` run (`AI.a_chat_run` → `SmolAgent.chat`) with: * a **step-scoped system message** (role + plan + notes + objective), * the step's `LoopGuard` limits from `policy.limits`, * `run_context` = the chat's `AgentRunContext` (so `ChatEventBridge` keeps persisting `tool_events` on the response message), * `current_chat` = the chat (budget enforcement inside `SmolAgent` stays active). After the step the engine asks the model for a **structured decision**: ```json { "action": "continue", "reason": "pagination implemented, tests pass" } { "action": "replan", "reason": "client uses a different fetch helper", "steps": [ { "title": "...", "objective": "...", "verification": "project_script" } ] } { "action": "ask_user", "question": "Should the default page_size be 20 or 50?", "options": ["20", "50"] } { "action": "finish", "summary": "Pagination added to API and client; tests pass" } { "action": "blocked", "reason": "the credentials for the staging API are missing" } ``` Invalid JSON is **not** fatal: the engine falls back to a deterministic decision (`continue` while steps remain and the step touched files; otherwise `finish` with the raw step output appended). This mirrors the tolerant JSON handling used by the remaining project code and guarantees the loop always terminates. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Step result
AgentRunResult"] --> B["Verify"] B --> C["Decision LLM call
temperature=0, JSON only"] C --> D{"parsed?"} D -->|no| E["Fallback decision
deterministic"] D -->|yes| F{"action"} E --> F F -->|continue| G["next pending step"] F -->|replan| H["rewrite plan (revision+1)"] F -->|ask_user| I["suspend → NEEDS_INPUT"] F -->|finish| J["COMPLETED"] F -->|blocked| K["BLOCKED"] ``` ## 11. Verification Verification is **deterministic first**, LLM second. | Strategy | Mechanism | Reuses | |---|---|---| | `none` | Step is trusted | — | | `project_script` | `settings.script_test` executed, output checked against `settings.script_test_check_regex` | `CodeEngine.project_script_test()` | | `custom_script` | `AgentVerificationSettings.script` | `exec_command` | | `llm_review` | Diff + step objective reviewed by the RAG model | `settings.get_rag_model()` | ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Step finished"] --> B{"verification.enabled?"} B -->|no| F["done"] B -->|yes| C["run project script / custom script"] C --> D{"failure regex matched?"} D -->|no| F D -->|yes| E{"attempts < max_attempts?"} E -->|yes| G["retry step with the failure output
as required fix"] E -->|no| H["mark step FAILED
decision = replan"] G --> C ``` Every attempt is recorded in `AgentStep.attempts` and the failure console output is truncated into `AgentVerification.output` — it is then injected verbatim into the retry prompt (the same technique the existing `code_engine` uses). ## 12. Interaction with the user (human-in-the-loop) The agent talks to the user through a dedicated **dual-response tool**, `ask_user`, and a **suspend/resume** mechanism. This is what turns a batch job into a colleague. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant AE as AgentEngine participant SA as SmolAgent participant T as ask_user tool participant B as ChatEventBridge participant S as AgentStateStore AE->>SA: run step N SA->>T: ask_user(question, options) T-->>B: TOOL_END (output = question) B->>U: message event (question rendered) T-->>SA: ToolResponse(llm_response="question sent; waiting") SA-->>AE: AgentRunResult AE->>S: persist AgentRunState (waiting_user + pending question) AE->>B: STEP_END (status=needs_input) + publish AE-->>U: run suspended (Chat.status = waiting_user) Note over U,AE: minutes or hours later U->>AE: next user message (the answer) AE->>S: load AgentRunState AE->>AE: match answer → pending question AE->>SA: resume step N with the answer injected SA-->>AE: continue ``` ### Contract | Aspect | Decision | |---|---| | Transport | `ask_user` tool → `ToolResponse.user_response` is the question, `llm_response` is the model-facing ack | | Suspension | The run stops at a **step boundary**; `AgentRunState.pending_question` is written *before* the run is marked `waiting_user` | | Resume trigger | The next `user` message on the same `chat.id` while `AgentRunState.status == waiting_user` | | Resume payload | The answer is injected as the tool result of the pending question (not as a new plan) | | Timeout | `ask_user.timeout_seconds` → `on_timeout` ∈ `keep_waiting` \| `use_default` \| `abort` | | Budget | Questions never count as steps; `max_questions_per_run` bounds them | | Idempotency | `question_id` is written in the state **and** stamped into `Message.meta_data`; a duplicated answer is ignored | | Restart safety | State is on disk (`AgentStateStore`), so a process restart still resumes | ### Confirmation of destructive tools `AgentBehavior.confirm_tools` reuses the same mechanism: before executing a listed tool, the engine emits a confirmation question. Denial feeds `"User denied this operation"` back to the model as the tool result, so it can choose another approach instead of failing the run.
Why a tool instead of a special "pause" instruction? class AgentCancelled(Exception):
    """Raised at checkpoints when the run has been cancelled."""


class InsufficientFundsError(Exception):
    """Raised by the wallet pre-flight check."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Cancellation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class CancellationToken:
    """Thread-safe cancellation token. cancel() may be called from any thread
    (e.g. a Socket.IO 'stop' handler) while the agent loop runs elsewhere."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._event = threading.Event()
        self.reason: str | None = None

    def cancel(self, reason: str = "user_requested"):
        self.reason = reason
        self._event.set()

    @property
    def cancelled(self) -> bool:
        return self._event.is_set()

    def raise_if_cancelled(self):
        if self._event.is_set():
            raise AgentCancelled(self.reason or "cancelled")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Events
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class AgentEventType(str, Enum):
    RUN_START = "run_start"
    RUN_END = "run_end"
    RUN_ERROR = "run_error"
    RUN_CANCELLED = "run_cancelled"
    LLM_REQUEST = "llm_request"
    LLM_CHUNK = "llm_chunk"
    LLM_USAGE = "llm_usage"
    TOOL_START = "tool_start"
    TOOL_END = "tool_end"
    TOOL_ERROR = "tool_error"
    TOOL_LOGS = "tool_logs"
    WALLET_CHECK = "wallet_check"


@dataclass
class AgentEvent:
    type: AgentEventType
    run_id: str
    project_id: str
    payload: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    ts: float = field(default_factory=time.time)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {"type": self.type.value, "run_id": self.run_id,
                "project_id": self.project_id, "ts": self.ts, **self.payload}

    prompt_tokens: int = 0
    completion_tokens: int = 0
    tool_calls: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # name -> {count, errors, total_ms}

    def on_event(self, event: AgentEvent):
        p = event.payload
        if event.type == AgentEventType.LLM_USAGE:
            self.prompt_tokens += p.get("prompt_tokens", 0)
            self.completion_tokens += p.get("completion_tokens", 0)
        elif event.type in (AgentEventType.TOOL_END, AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR):
            stats = self.tool_calls.setdefault(

            stats["count"] += 1
            stats["total_ms"] += p.get("duration_ms", 0.0)
            if event.type == AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR:

"""
ChatEventBridge — attaches AgentRunContext events to the chat response message
and persists it on EVERY change (crash-safe).

During an AI turn the SmolAgent emits :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentEvent`
notifications (tool start/end/error, run lifecycle).

Events are ASSOCIATED with the assistant **response message** that the
ChatEngine created BEFORE calling the AI — they are never emitted as separate
chat messages:

    * ``response_message.tool_events``      → list of :class:`ToolEvent`
      (one entry per tool call, updated in place: running → done/error). Each
      event also carries the tool's user-facing ``output`` so tool output can be
      rendered collapsed/hidden instead of polluting ``Message.content``.
    * ``response_message.lifecycle_events`` → list of :class:`LifeCycleEvent`
      (one entry per agent run, updated in place)

Tool output
-----------
TOOL_END events carry the dual-response tool's user-facing ``output``
(``ToolResponse.user_response``). The bridge stores it on the matching
:class:`ToolEvent` (``ToolEvent.output``) instead of it being merged into the
chat content, so the client decides how to display it. Cached tool calls do not
re-emit output (the first execution already delivered it).

Crash-safety guarantee
----------------------
On every event change the response message is:

    1. **Persisted immediately** via the ChatManager granular merge-safe
       methods (``add_message`` on first change, ``update_message`` after).
       If the process dies mid-run, every event received so far — including
       tool errors, run errors and aggregated analytics — is already on disk.
    2. **Streamed** to clients in real time via the EventManager so the UI
       can render tool progress live.

ADDED — streamed-chunk crash-safety (:meth:`maybe_persist_stream`):
    Streaming callbacks may call :meth:`maybe_persist_stream` on every flush;
    the bridge persists the response message AT MOST once per
    ``STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` (monotonic clock). A hard kill
    therefore loses at most that many seconds of streamed partial text while
    keeping disk I/O bounded.

ADDED — auxiliary message crash-safety (:meth:`persist_message`):
    Any auxiliary message produced mid-run (e.g. hidden reasoning messages)
    can be persisted immediately and idempotently. Persisted ``doc_id``s are
    tracked bridge-side so the first call inserts (``add_message``) and later
    calls update (``update_message``).

ADDED — defensive ChatManager fallback:
    The idempotency guarantee assumes ``ChatManager.update_message`` matches
    by ``doc_id``. If the granular methods are missing or fail, the bridge
    falls back to a coarse ``save_chat`` full write (after making sure the
    message is on the in-memory chat) so information is never silently lost.

The engine reuses :meth:`publish` on its own error / cancellation paths so
``response_message.error`` and ``cancelled_at`` are also persisted the moment
they are known, not only at the end of the turn.

Budget: the main task owns the money > "The main task will define the full task budget so the sum of all tasks cost > must not exceed it." The budget is a **tree**, not a per-chat number. `Chat.estimation_cost` already exists and `SmolAgent` already refuses to spend beyond it, so the engine builds the tree using that same field at every level. ```mermaid flowchart TD MAIN["Main task chat
estimation_cost = T (total budget)"] MAIN -->|own spend| OWN["main.cost"] MAIN -->|allocate| S1["step task #1
estimation_cost = a1"] MAIN -->|allocate| S2["step task #2
estimation_cost = a2"] MAIN -.->|next step| S3["step task #3
allocation when needed"] S1 -->|cost| R["rollup"] S2 -->|cost| R OWN --> R R --> AV["available = T - own - Σchildren - reserved"] AV -->|child_share| NEXT["a(next) = clamp(available * share, min, available)"] ``` ### Formulas ```text total = main.estimation_cost (declared by the main task) spent = main.cost + Σ children.cost (monotonic, deletion-safe) reserved = Σ allocations of running children (in-flight reservations) available = total - spent - reserved allocation(child) = clamp(available * child_share, min_child_budget, available) ``` with `child_share = 0.35` and `min_child_budget` global defaults (profile/task may only **narrow** them). ### Enforcement (three independent layers) | Layer | Where | Effect | |---|---|---| | **Chat budget** | `SmolAgent._cost_limit_exceeded` on the **step task** | The step cannot exceed its own `estimation_cost` → no child can overspend its allocation | | **Reservation** | `AgentEngine` before starting a step | Two concurrent steps can never both claim the same remaining money | | **Rollup + stopper** | `AgentBudget.available` before each step | The tree stops before exceeding `total` → `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` / stopper rule | Because `Chat.cost` is **monotonic** (deleting messages does not refund), the tree budget can never be "reset" by editing the chat history. ### Extension flow When the budget is exhausted the run does not just die: the `budget` stopper rule sends an `ask_user` question with the numbers and the options (`extend_budget` / `reduce_scope` / `accept_partial` / `stop`). Choosing `extend_budget` raises `main.estimation_cost` by the requested amount, bounded by `AgentSettings.max_budget_extensions` and `max_budget_extension_cxjcoins` per run (audited in `AgentRunState.stoppers`).
Why allocation instead of one shared pool? A shared pool requires a global lock and makes concurrent runs fight each other. Allocation turns the tree constraint into a **local invariant** that the already existing `SmolAgent` budget check enforces by itself, with no new concurrency code in the hot path. The pool view is recomputed cheaply at each step boundary by summing `Chat.cost` of the children.

It is *not* the stop reason: the reason is the outcome, the stopper is the trigger. Stopper conditions are declared in **two places**: | Source | Field | Role | |---|---|---| | **Profile** | `Profile.agent.stoppers` (defaults + rules) | what this kind of agent needs from humans in general | | **Main task** | `Chat.agent_task.stoppers` (overrides) | what *this* request needs | Precedence: **task overrides profile**, profile overrides global defaults. A task can change the *action* and the *question*, but it can never allow exceeding the hard limits (permissions, guardrails, platform caps). ### Condition catalogue | Condition | Detected when | Default action | |---|---|---| | `ambiguity` | planning/step needs a decision that changes the outcome | `ask_user` | | `missing_dependency` | a required credential/file/service is not available | `ask_user` | | `destructive` | a tool in `confirm_tools` is about to run | `ask_user` | | `plan_review` | plan ready and `confirm_plan` enabled | `ask_user` | | `budget` | `available <= 0` (§14) | `ask_user` (extend / reduce / partial / stop) | | `step_limit` | `usage.steps >= limits.max_steps` | `ask_user` | | `round_limit` | `LoopGuard` stopped the step | `finish` (step-level, summarised) | | `wall_clock` | run exceeded `max_wall_clock_seconds` | `pause` (resumable later) | | `verification_failed` | attempts exhausted on a step | `ask_user` (retry / accept / replan) | | `no_progress` | N identical decisions or N steps without changes | `ask_user` | | `guardrail` | input/output/tool blocked by `GuardrailService` | `fail` | | `user_requested` | human pressed *pause* / *stop* | `pause` / `stop` (§16) | | `error` | provider or unrecoverable exception | `fail` | ### Resolution ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Condition detected"] --> B{"rule in Chat.agent_task.stoppers?"} B -->|yes| C["use it"] B -->|no| D{"rule in Profile.agent.stoppers?"} D -->|yes| C D -->|no| E["global default
AgentSettings.stopper_action_default"] E --> C C --> F{"action"} F -->|ask_user| G["AgentQuestion
status = WAITING_USER"] F -->|pause| H["AgentPause
status = PAUSED"] F -->|finish| I["final report + COMPLETED/PARTIAL"] F -->|fail| J["BLOCKED / FAILED"] ``` ### How the agent talks to the human The agent has **three channels** to the human; all of them reuse the existing tool-event pipeline (`TOOL_END.output`) so nothing new is needed in the client. | Channel | When | Mechanism | |---|---|---| | **Mid-step question** | the model decides it needs an answer (`ask_user` tool) | tool returns a dual response: question to the user, `waiting` ack to the model | | **Stopper dialogue** | a stopper condition fires with action `ask_user` | engine emits `ask_user` **outside** the step, with options derived from the condition | | **Task card state** | always | the step card moves columns and its content states what is blocking | ### Stopper dialogue (sequence) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AE as AgentEngine participant R as Stopper rule participant B as ChatEventBridge participant S as AgentStateStore participant CM as ChatManager participant U as Human AE->>R: condition = budget (available = 0) R->>AE: action = ask_user, options AE->>AE: hit = AgentStopperHit(condition, action) AE->>B: QUESTION_ASKED(condition, question, options) B->>CM: update_message (tool_events output) B->>U: message event (question + buttons) AE->>S: persist state (WAITING_USER, question, stoppers[]) AE->>CM: save_chat(main.status = waiting_user) Note over U,AE: human decides (minutes or hours) U->>AE: next user message: "extend_budget 0.5" AE->>S: load state, match question_id AE->>AE: apply decision (raise budget / reduce scope / accept partial) AE->>B: QUESTION_ANSWERED AE->>CM: save_chat(main.status = in_progress) AE->>AE: continue from the same step ``` ### Rules | Aspect | Decision | |---|---| | Where the answer goes | It is **not** injected into the step's prompt blindly: the engine interprets it (`extend_budget`, `accept_partial`, ...) and only then continues or replans | | Answer transport | The next `user` message on the **same chat** (or an explicit `resume(answer=...)` API call) | | Options | Rendered as `AgentQuestion.options`; free text always allowed (`allow_free_text`) | | Timeout | `ask_user.timeout_seconds` → `keep_waiting` (default) / `use_default` / `abort` | | Continuations | `max_continuations` bounds how many times the human may "continue anyway" per condition, so a loop of ask→extend→ask cannot happen | | Audit | Every hit is appended to `AgentRunState.stoppers` and rendered in the final report | | Cheap conditions | `round_limit` and similar non-blocking conditions are handled with `finish` (report + partial work), never by asking |
Why a stopper rule instead of a hardcoded if/else? Because the same condition needs different handling per agent: a `software_developer` must ask before spending more money, while a `documentation_writer` should simply finish with what it has. Keeping the mapping in data (profile + task) keeps the engine dumb and testable, and lets a single request override the policy without touching code.

partial result kept"] C --> D["run CANCELLED"] P -->|resume| E["continue from next step"] P -->|stop| D ``` * **Pause** is honoured **only at a step boundary** (between steps, after verification).
